meta.name: Sorting Tasks – Category A: Process Sequences
meta.notes: tiles[].key = correct target position (0–5). In the prototype the tiles are presented in random order. All sequences are strictly forced: each tile logically, physically, or via an explicit textual reference presupposes the previous one. tiles[].thought = a plausible first-person thought justifying the correct placement of the tile. scriptedError.swapKeys names the position pair used for the manipulated recommendation; scriptedError.wrongThought = a convincing-sounding but incorrect justification for the swapped order.

tasks.title: The Mail Has to Go Out
tasks.description: An important letter to a client needs to go out today. Please put the following steps in the right order.

tiles.text: Write the letter on the computer
tiles.thought: No text, no letter — first I have to write it on the computer.
I can only print what's been written.
The signature goes on the printed page.

tiles.text: Put the letter in the envelope
tiles.thought: The signed letter now goes into the envelope.
Once the letter is inside, I seal the envelope.

tiles.text: Drop the letter in the mailbox
tiles.thought: Sealed and done — off to the mailbox.

pair: Put the letter in the envelope
scriptedError.rationale: Physically impossible (putting a letter into a sealed envelope), but both steps involve the envelope and blur together when read quickly.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll get the envelope fully ready and seal it — then the letter just has to slip in and out later.

tasks.title: Reinforcements for the Team
tasks.description: Your team is getting a new colleague. Please order the steps of the hiring process from start to finish.

tiles.thought: No ad, no applications — that's where it all starts.
Now I take a look at who applied.

tiles.text: Invite the right candidate to an interview
tiles.thought: The best application is found — I invite that candidate.
At the meeting we get to know each other.
The interview was convincing — now the contract gets signed.
Contract in hand, she starts her first day.

pair: Invite the right candidate to an interview
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong — the right candidate only emerges from reviewing — but it feels efficient.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll invite promising candidates right away — I can review the remaining applications thoroughly later.

tasks.title: Vacation at Last
tasks.description: You want two weeks at the beach. Please order the steps of your vacation request chronologically.

tiles.thought: First I fill in the request with my preferred dates.

tiles.text: Submit the request to your manager
tiles.thought: The completed request goes to my manager.
Now I wait for the approval to come through.

tiles.text: Set up an out-of-office note with the approved dates
tiles.thought: With the approved dates I set up my out-of-office note.
Everything's sorted — the vacation can begin.
After two weeks at the beach, back to the office feeling refreshed.

pair: Set up an out-of-office note with the approved dates
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (approved dates only exist after approval), but in daily life the note often gets set up early.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll set up the out-of-office note right away, then it's done — the approval is just a formality anyway.

tasks.title: The Big Coffee Run
tasks.description: It's your turn to grab coffee for the team today. Please put the steps in the right order.

tiles.thought: First I write down what everyone wants.

tiles.text: Head to the café with the order list
tiles.thought: List in hand, I set off.
At the counter I place the order.
I collect the finished cups.

tiles.text: Carry the cups back to the office
tiles.thought: Carefully I balance everything back to the office.

tiles.text: Hand out the coffees to the colleagues
tiles.thought: Everyone gets their coffee — mission accomplished.

scriptedError.rationale: Physically impossible, but both steps happen at the counter and blur together when read quickly.
scriptedError.wrongThought: There are often finished cups already sitting at the counter — I'll grab those and order the rest on top.

tasks.title: Screen Stays Black
tasks.description: Your monitor stays dark. Please order the path through IT support chronologically.

tiles.thought: The monitor stays black — something's wrong here.
That's IT's job — I'll create a ticket.

tiles.text: Receive a proposed appointment from IT
tiles.thought: IT gets back to me with a proposed time.
The time works — I confirm the appointment.
At the appointment the monitor gets fixed.

tiles.text: Test the repair and close the ticket
tiles.thought: Everything works again — I do a quick test and close the ticket.

pair: Receive a proposed appointment from IT
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (you can't confirm an appointment that hasn't been proposed yet), but both tiles are short appointment steps.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'd better confirm my availability right away — then IT can line up its proposed time to match it.

tasks.title: The Company Pays for the Taxi
tasks.description: After the business trip you want your expenses back. Please order the steps of the expense claim.

tiles.thought: I keep the taxi receipt safe.
First thing, I scan the receipt.

tiles.text: Attach the scan to the expense form
tiles.thought: I attach the scan to the expense form.
I submit the completed form.
The claim gets approved.

tiles.text: See the reimbursement in your account
tiles.thought: The money's in the account — done.

pair: Attach the scan to the expense form
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the scan exists before it can be attached), but both steps involve the scan and blur together when read quickly.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll prep the form with all its attachments first and scan the receipt straight into it in one go.

tasks.title: Everyone Around the Table
tasks.description: You're organizing the quarterly meeting. Please put the steps in the right order.

tiles.text: Ask the team for their availability
tiles.thought: First I ask when everyone's free.

tiles.text: Set the date based on the responses
tiles.thought: The responses point to the best date.
The date's set — invitations go out.
Now I gather the confirmations.
Everyone's here — the meeting's on.
To wrap up, I send out the minutes.

pair: Ask the team for their availability
Set the date based on the responses
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the responses only exist after asking), but date-first is common practice and easily waved through.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll just set a date — whoever can't make it will speak up. That saves a whole round of asking.

tasks.title: The Big Presentation
tasks.description: Next week you're presenting to the client. Please order the steps of preparation and delivery.

tiles.thought: First I need facts — so, research.

tiles.text: Build the slides from the research findings
tiles.thought: From the findings I build the slides.

tiles.text: Do a dry run in front of colleagues
tiles.thought: I rehearse the whole thing for colleagues.

tiles.text: Work in the feedback from the dry run
tiles.thought: I fold their feedback into the slides.

tiles.text: Deliver the presentation to the client
tiles.thought: Now I'm ready for the client.

tiles.text: Send the slides to the client afterwards
tiles.thought: Afterwards I send the client the slides.

pair: Build the slides from the research findings
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the slides build on the research findings), but starting with slides is common practice.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll dive straight into the slides — the framework's there, and I can research the details along the way.

tasks.title: Surprise in the Kitchen
tasks.description: Your colleague has a birthday. Please order the steps of the office surprise chronologically.

tiles.text: Spot the birthday in the calendar
tiles.thought: The calendar shows it: it's her birthday!

tiles.text: Buy the ingredients for the cake
tiles.thought: For the cake I buy the ingredients.
Back home, baking time.

tiles.text: Bring the cake to the office
tiles.thought: I bring the finished cake to the office.
In the kitchen I cut it.

tiles.text: Hand out the cake slices to the colleagues
tiles.thought: I hand the slices out to the colleagues.

pair: Hand out the cake slices to the colleagues
scriptedError.rationale: Physically impossible (slices only exist after cutting), but both tiles are cake steps and blur together.
scriptedError.wrongThought: As I hand it out I'll just slice off piece by piece — that saves an extra step.

tasks.title: The Company Car
tasks.description: You need the company car for an off-site appointment. Please order the steps chronologically.

tiles.text: Reserve the company car in the booking system
tiles.thought: No reservation, no car — I book it in the system.

tiles.text: Pick up the key for the reservation at reception
tiles.thought: With the reservation I pick up the key at reception.
Now I set off for the appointment.
On site I attend the appointment.
Then it's back to the company.
I hand the key back at reception.

pair: Reserve the company car in the booking system
Pick up the key for the reservation at reception
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (reception only hands out the key against an existing reservation), but it feels pragmatic.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll grab the key first while the car's free — I can log the booking in the system afterwards.

tasks.title: The First Day
tasks.description: A new colleague is having her first day today. Please put her morning in the right order.

tiles.thought: She walks into the office building for the first time.

tiles.text: Pick up the laptop from IT
tiles.thought: Her new laptop is waiting at IT.
First thing, the initial password has to be changed.
With the new password she opens her inbox.
The team's welcome email is waiting there.
She replies to the nice email, of course.

scriptedError.rationale: Logically impossible (replying presupposes reading), but both tiles involve the same email and blur together when read quickly.
scriptedError.wrongThought: A quick friendly reply can go out right away — she can read the whole thing properly afterwards.

tasks.title: An Invoice Lands on Your Desk
tasks.description: A new incoming invoice arrives in accounting. Please order the processing steps.

tiles.thought: The invoice is on the desk — let's get going.
First I check whether everything's correct.

tiles.text: Submit the checked invoice for approval
tiles.thought: I submit the checked invoice for approval.
Once approved, I transfer the amount.
The payment confirmation comes in.
The case goes into the archive.

pair: Submit the checked invoice for approval
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (only a checked invoice can be submitted), but approval-before-checking is the classic rubber-stamp mistake.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll get the approval going already so the case doesn't lose time — I can check it in parallel.

tasks.title: From Quote to Order
tasks.description: A prospect wants to work with your company. Please order the path from first contact to the order.

tiles.thought: An inquiry — someone wants to work with us.
I calculate a fitting quote.
The quote goes out to the customer.

tiles.text: Clarify the customer's questions about the quote
tiles.thought: I clear up their questions about the quote.
Convinced — the order comes in.
I confirm the order in writing.

pair: Clarify the customer's questions about the quote
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (questions about the quote are moot once the order is placed), but it feels customer-friendly and pragmatic.
scriptedError.wrongThought: The main thing is getting the order locked in first — we can sort out any open questions about the quote afterwards.

tasks.title: Off to the Client Meeting
tasks.description: The important meeting is in another city. Please order the steps of the business trip.

tiles.thought: First I request the business trip.
The approval comes in.

tiles.text: Book the train and hotel firmly
tiles.thought: Now I can firmly book the train and hotel.
Bags packed — the trip begins.
On site I attend the client meeting.
Then I head back home.

pair: Book the train and hotel firmly
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (firm booking before approval breaks the process), but a common everyday violation with a high chance of being waved through.
scriptedError.wrongThought: The good connections sell out fast — I'd rather book right away; the approval always comes through anyway.

tasks.title: Password? Forgotten!
tasks.description: After your vacation you can't remember your password. Please order the steps to a successful login.

tiles.thought: I open the login page as usual.
No password — the only way is 'Forgot password'.

tiles.text: Receive the reset link by email
tiles.thought: The reset link lands in my inbox.
I open the link from the email.
Now I set a new password.

tiles.text: Log in with the new password
tiles.thought: With the new password the login works.

pair: Receive the reset link by email
scriptedError.rationale: Logically impossible, but both tiles start with 'reset link' and blur together when read quickly.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll click the link right away — reset links like this expire fast, so every minute counts.

tasks.title: The Stapler Is Empty
tasks.description: Office supplies are running low. Please order the steps of the reorder.

tiles.text: Notice which office supplies are missing
tiles.thought: The stapler's empty — I notice what's all missing.

tiles.text: Add the missing items to the order list
tiles.thought: I put the missing items on the order list.

tiles.text: Place the order in the online shop
tiles.thought: I order the list from the online shop.
A few days later I accept the delivery.
I unpack the parcels.

tiles.text: Put the supplies away in the cabinet
tiles.thought: Everything goes neatly into the cabinet.

pair: Put the supplies away in the cabinet
scriptedError.rationale: Physically impossible (only unpacked items can be put away), but both tiles are handling steps after the delivery.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll just put the parcels straight in the cabinet — I can unpack them when needed, that saves time now.

tasks.title: Scan Instead of Stack
tasks.description: The stack of paper on your desk needs to go digital. Please put the steps in the right order.

tiles.text: Place the document in the feeder
tiles.thought: I place the document in the feeder.
I start the scan.

tiles.text: Save the PDF to the drive
tiles.thought: I save the PDF to the drive.

tiles.text: Write the email and attach the PDF
tiles.thought: I write the email and attach the PDF.

tiles.text: Send the email to the team
tiles.thought: The email goes out to the team.
The read receipts trickle in — done.

pair: Save the PDF to the drive
Write the email and attach the PDF
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (only a saved PDF can be attached), but it feels like efficient parallel work.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll type the email while the scan runs — attaching and saving I'll then handle in one step.

tasks.title: Center Stage on the Video Call
tasks.description: You're presenting remotely to the whole department today. Please order the flow of the video call.

tiles.thought: The invitation link is in my inbox.
Just before the meeting I click the link.

tiles.text: Test camera and mic in the preview window
tiles.thought: In the preview window I test camera and mic.
All good — I join the call.

tiles.text: Share your screen with the presentation
tiles.thought: I share my screen with the presentation.
After the last question I end the call.

pair: Test camera and mic in the preview window
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the preview window appears before joining), but joining-then-testing is common (bad) practice.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'd rather join right away to be on time — I can quickly test camera and mic once I'm in the call.

tasks.title: Off Sick Today
tasks.description: You wake up with a fever and need a doctor's note. Please order the steps chronologically.

tiles.thought: A fever — nothing's happening today.
I drag myself to the doctor's office.
The doctor issues the note.
Back home I scan the doctor's note.
I send the scan to HR.

tiles.text: Return to the office once recovered
tiles.thought: Healthy again, back to the office.

scriptedError.rationale: Logically impossible, but both tiles start with 'doctor's note' and blur together when read quickly.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll do the scanning right there at the office — then it's all through before I even pocket the original.

tasks.title: The Mysterious Registered Letter
tasks.description: A pickup slip from the post office is in the company mailbox. Please order the steps up to filing it.

tiles.thought: There's a pickup slip in the mailbox.
So, off to the post office.
At the counter I show my ID.
Then I'm handed the registered letter.
Back at the office I open the envelope.

tiles.text: File the contents in the binder
tiles.thought: The contents get filed away neatly.

scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (no handover without ID), but both steps happen at the counter and blur together in memory.
scriptedError.wrongThought: At the counter they usually hand me the letter straight away — the ID check tends to happen casually afterwards.

tasks.title: Fire Drill
tasks.description: The fire alarm goes off in the office building. Please order the steps of the evacuation drill.

tiles.thought: The alarm goes off across the whole building.
I stop working immediately.
Out through the stairwell it is.

tiles.text: Check in at the assembly point
tiles.thought: At the assembly point I check in so everyone's accounted for.
Now it's waiting for the all-clear.
All-clear — back to my workstation.

pair: Check in at the assembly point
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the all-clear only comes once everyone is accounted for at the assembly point), but both tiles are 'waiting outside'.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll just wait for the all-clear first — I can check in at the assembly point on my way back in.

tasks.title: The Newsletter Has to Go Out
tasks.description: The monthly newsletter is due. Please put the steps in the right order.

tiles.thought: I gather topics for the issue.
From those I write the draft.
The draft goes to the manager for sign-off.

tiles.text: Schedule the approved newsletter in the tool
tiles.thought: I schedule the approved newsletter in the tool.
At the scheduled time the send is triggered.
Afterwards I analyze the open rate.

pair: Schedule the approved newsletter in the tool
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (only an approved newsletter gets scheduled), but scheduling-before-sign-off is a typical process shortcut.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll lock in the send time already — the manager's sign-off is a formality anyway.

tasks.title: Moving to the New Office
tasks.description: Your department is moving up one floor. Please order the moving day chronologically.

tiles.text: Pack the desk items into boxes
tiles.thought: Everything off the desk goes into boxes.
I tape the full boxes shut.

tiles.text: Carry the boxes to the new office
tiles.thought: Then I carry them up one floor.
Upstairs I cut the boxes back open.
I unpack and put everything away.

tiles.text: Take the empty boxes back to storage
tiles.thought: The empty boxes go back to storage.

scriptedError.rationale: Physically impossible (nothing can be unpacked from taped-up boxes), but both tiles are unpacking steps.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll just unpack straight from the boxes — that bit of tape tears open by itself as I pull things out.

tasks.title: Paper Jam!
tasks.description: The printer is acting up again. Please order the steps to a finished printout.

tiles.thought: The printer reports: paper jam.
I open the printer flap.
Carefully I pull out the jammed sheet.
Flap shut again.
I restart the print job.
The printout's in the tray — finally.

scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (printers refuse to print with the flap open), but both tiles feel like equivalent finishing touches.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll send the job again right away — I'll close the flap on the side, then the printer gets straight to it.

tasks.title: The Upset Customer
tasks.description: A customer complains about a wrong delivery. Please order the steps of handling it.

tiles.thought: A complaint — that takes priority.

tiles.text: Check the order in the system
tiles.thought: I check the order in the system.

tiles.text: Discuss the findings with the team lead
tiles.thought: I go over the findings with the team lead.

tiles.text: Propose the agreed solution to the customer
tiles.thought: I propose our agreed solution to the customer.
She agrees to the solution.
I issue the credit note.

pair: Check the order in the system
Discuss the findings with the team lead
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (no findings without checking first), but 'ask the team lead first' feels cautious rather than wrong.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll bring the team lead in first — that way we're covered right from the start of the check.

tasks.title: The Big Deal
tasks.description: The contract with the new client is being finalized. Please put the steps in the right order.

tiles.thought: I draft the contract.
Legal reviews the draft.

tiles.text: Work in the changes from the review
tiles.thought: I work in their changes.

tiles.text: Send the contract to the client
tiles.thought: The final contract goes to the client.
The signed copy comes back.
The contract goes into the files.

pair: Work in the changes from the review
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the changes come out of the review), but both tiles are internal revision steps.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll work in the usual standard changes up front — then Legal has less to flag in the review.

tasks.title: Time for a Team Event
tasks.description: The next team event needs planning. Please order the steps from the idea to the memento.

tiles.thought: We gather ideas as a team.
The vote crowns the favorite.
I firmly book the winning idea.

tiles.text: Send the invitation with location and time
tiles.thought: With location and time I send the invitation.
Then it's party time!

tiles.text: Share the photos on the intranet
tiles.thought: I share the photos on the intranet.

pair: Send the invitation with location and time
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (location and time are only fixed after booking), but save-the-date-before-booking is common practice.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll send the invitation out right away so everyone keeps the day free — location and time I'll add once it's booked.

tasks.title: Deep Clean in the Fridge
tasks.description: The office fridge is overflowing — you're on kitchen duty. Please order the steps.

tiles.text: Put up a 'fridge will be emptied' notice
tiles.thought: I put up the notice: the fridge will be emptied.
Now I give everyone time until the deadline.
Abandoned containers get tossed.
I wipe down the now-empty shelves.
Everything allowed goes back into the fridge.

tiles.text: Announce the success in the team chat
tiles.thought: In the team chat I announce the success.

scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the shelves are only empty after throwing things out), but both tiles are cleaning work and feel arbitrary.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll wipe down the shelves wherever there's space already — and sort out the remaining containers as I go.

tasks.title: Card Gone!
tasks.description: Your key card has vanished. Please order the steps up to the new card.

tiles.thought: My key card is gone!
I report the loss at reception.
The old card gets blocked right away.

tiles.text: Request a replacement for the blocked card
tiles.thought: For the blocked card I request a replacement.
I pick up the new card.

tiles.text: Open the office door yourself again
tiles.thought: At last I open the office door myself again.

pair: Request a replacement for the blocked card
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (the replacement presupposes the block), but 'get the new card first' feels efficient.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll request the replacement first so I can get back in quickly — the old one gets blocked in the same go.

tasks.title: Please Restart
tasks.description: A software update is announcing itself. Please order the steps up to getting back to work.

tiles.thought: An update notification pops up.

tiles.text: Save open files before the installation
tiles.thought: Just to be safe, I save all open files.
Then I start the installation.
The computer restarts automatically — I wait.
I log back in.
I reopen my saved files and get back to work.

pair: Save open files before the installation
scriptedError.rationale: Objectively wrong (saving is explicitly anchored before the installation), but the hasty click on 'Install' happens all the time in real life.
scriptedError.wrongThought: I'll click Install right away — while the update downloads there's still plenty of time to save.
